newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX slips in bourse on weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: German DAX slips in bourse on weaker dollar.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index opened sharply lower on Friday following an overnight decline on Wall Street and some pressure on the dollar, but volumes were expected to be thin over the session.
Dealers said the market lacked clear direction going into the weekend and was somewhat uncertain ahead of an expiry deadline this session for options on the DAX index and some of its constituents.
The 30-share DAX was down 37.84 points, or 1.12 percent, at 3,345.41 points early on.
"We haven't had any real orders," said a trader at a large Frankfurt bank. "Things are just creaking along."
There were few outstanding movements among blue chip shares. Chemical giant Hoechst AG was sharply lower, down 1.95 marks or 2.93 percent at 64.50 marks.
Dealers linked Hoechst's decline with presentations the company had made to investors in London, while the lower dollar also contributed to the fall.
Other chemical stocks lower in early bourse included BASF AG, which was down 1.60 marks, or 2.37 percent, at 65.90.
Daimler-Benz AG, another decliner from Thursday, was also under pressure, down 75 pfennigs at 132.55 marks.
BMW AG and Porsche AG, two darlings of the stock market in recent weeks, were both sharply lower in early bourse, as sentiment in car shares was hit by the lower dollar.
BMW was down 33 marks, or 2.31 percent, at 1,398 marks, while Porsche was down 50 marks, or 2.35 percent, at 1,080 marks.
